lessons: A cap that admits a name because it fell is not telling you the name got better. Petronas Chemicals went from one lot to two by losing 6.54%, and the round trip got worse on the smaller ticket; reading that arithmetic as permission inverts a risk control.

The same shape of evidence points both ways and is worth no more in either direction. 'Rises to three-month high' and 'leads Bursa losers' are both price observations with no body, and a book that refuses the first must refuse the second.

A macro event the system cannot represent should be recorded as a gap, not narrated as context. The Fed hiked; this book has no rate input and no tested rule, and saying so is more useful than a paragraph about what rate rises usually do.

An announced review that produces no collected outcome stays unresolved. The government meeting on electricity bills was convened for today and the collector caught nothing from it - which is why the previous page was right not to treat the announcement as a resolution.

A vintage can make an old reading stronger and a new price harder to explain at the same time. Brent's move above 120 became knowable today, so the crude leg under Petronas Chemicals' run is better evidenced than it was - and the name fell 6.54% anyway.
